findings.detail: The manifest records `head 88e29193` (HEAD~1) while HEAD is 913d1e78, and every consequence is checkable from the checkout. (a) Rule 3 content binding: attested `.apexyard/metrics.json` is 4a6d78c2 but `HEAD:.apexyard/metrics.json` is e4e6feaa; `.apexyard/review.json` is ec1fa48b vs c9a8db81; `scripts/verify-evidence.mjs` is fa97e9bd vs b723c409. (b) `scripts/verify-attestation.mjs` is attested at line 48 but was deleted in HEAD, which trips "was reviewed but is absent at HEAD". (c) Coverage: `tsconfig.json` and `docs/quality/architecture-review-2026-08-03.md` both changed in d730c7b...HEAD and appear nowhere in the manifest, so `uncoveredPaths` reports them as changed-but-never-reviewed. (d) `gateSatisfied(fields, 'high')` reads `findings high=2` and emits "2 unresolved high finding(s)"; `.apexyard/review.json` also carries `verdict: request_changes`. The `Evidence bundle` job is a documented HARD GATE and the `ci` aggregate job treats anything but `success` as failure, so this PR cannot go green as committed — and the failure text will point at the wrong thing ("changed after it was reviewed") rather than at "the review was never re-run for this commit".
findings.summary: The committed evidence bundle describes HEAD~1, so this PR's own CI gate fails

findings.detail: `EXCLUDED` drops only `.apexyard/attestation`, its `.sig`, and `allowed_signers`. Every other bundle artifact stays in the attested set — the committed manifest proves it, listing `.apexyard/accessibility-report.json`, `architecture.json`, `attestation.json`, `dependency-report.json`, `findings.json`, `metrics.json`, `review-summary.md`, and `review.json` at lines 11-18. Meanwhile `verify-evidence.mjs:181` excludes the whole `.apexyard/` prefix, but ONLY from the coverage check; the rule 3 content-binding loop at lines 157-174 has no such exclusion and walks all of `fields.files`. Since `evidence.mjs` rewrites all seven artifacts on every run, the sequence is: review at HEAD_n attests bundle blobs B_n -> `evidence.mjs` writes B_n+1 -> stage 11 passes locally because HEAD has not moved -> the maintainer commits B_n+1 -> CI now sees attested OID B_n against actual B_n+1 and reports "changed after it was reviewed". The next local run then fails verify-evidence, re-runs the review, and repeats. This is precisely the "no fixed point" defect the commit message and docs/quality/architecture-review-2026-08-03.md:60 claim to have closed by deleting the second verifier; deleting it aligned the coverage exclusion but left the content-binding asymmetry untouched, which is why the bundle currently on disk is stale. Neither bash suite catches it: the test-evidence.sh fixture (scripts/tests/test-evidence.sh:57-70) never commits a regenerated bundle, so the only path that reaches this state is untested.
findings.summary: The bundle's own artifacts are inside the attested scope, so the gate has no fixed point

findings.detail: gitattributes resolves each attribute from the LAST matching line. Line 20 unsets `text` for `.apexyard/attestation.sig` specifically to keep git from touching the signature's bytes, and line 22's `* text=auto` then matches the same path and re-sets `text`, silently undoing it. An SSH signature is base64 ASCII, so `text=auto` classifies it as text and a Windows clone with `core.autocrlf=true` gets CRLF — breaking `ssh-keygen -Y verify` on a machine that did nothing wrong, which is the exact failure line 15's comment says the `-text` prevents. The `eol=lf` pins on lines 3-6 and 16-19 survive (eol is a separate attribute and implies text), so only the binary exemption is affected. Low rather than medium only because no `.sig` is tracked today and no signer is registered (TD-028); it becomes a real, hard-to-diagnose failure the day signing is enabled per TD-027's revisit trigger.
findings.summary: Trailing `* text=auto` overrides the `-text` exemption on attestation.sig

findings.detail: `json.filter(...).map((f) => toPosixRelative(f.filePath, root)).sort().length` computes a full list of relativised, sorted paths and discards all of it, keeping only the count. The `.map` and `.sort` are dead work — a leftover from when this field returned the path list — and it is the only caller that makes `toPosixRelative`'s `root` argument load-bearing here. No correctness impact (the count is right), but it reads as though the paths matter, which invites someone to "fix" the field by returning the array and quietly changing the artifact schema.
findings.summary: files_with_findings builds and sorts an array only to take its length

findings.detail: Lines 128-129 say "Skipping this file is not cosmetic: it necessarily contains every pattern it searches for, so including it guarantees a self-match", and line 153 says "Skipping the pattern-list lines themselves, now that the file is in scope." Neither happens: `list_scan_targets` (lines 110-114) is `git ls-files` plus untracked-not-ignored with no exclusion, and nothing filters the `patterns=(...)` lines. Lines 102-109 argue at length for the opposite behaviour — that the file is deliberately in scope because every pattern has a `[` after its prefix and so cannot match itself. The three comments cannot all be true, and in a file whose whole purpose is that "a pattern that quietly stops matching is exactly the failure a scan should catch", a comment describing a filter that does not exist is the same class of hazard one level up.
findings.summary: Stale comments claim the scanner skips itself, which lines 102-109 explicitly reject

findings.detail: The header says the two CLIs consuming this module are `scripts/attest-review.mjs` and `scripts/verify-attestation.mjs`. The second was deleted in this same commit. It is now the only dangling reference to the removed file outside the (stale) bundle artifacts and the deliberate historical notes in verify-evidence.mjs:9, ADR-0002:96, and the architecture review — those three describe the removal on purpose; this one describes the file as current. A reader following it looks for a script that is not there.
findings.summary: Type declaration header still names the deleted verify-attestation.mjs

findings.detail: The HEAD commit message says "Also dropped `baseUrl` from tsconfig" and docs/quality/architecture-review-2026-08-03.md:82 records it under "Acted on today / FIXED: a deprecation". `"baseUrl": "."` is still on line 18. The diff added the explanatory comment on lines 19-21 ("No baseUrl: it is deprecated in TS 6 and removed in 7") without removing the setting it describes, and the older TD-001 comment on lines 15-17 still asserts the opposite — that baseUrl is what mirrors the `xlsx` alias. There is no behavioural difference today (`paths` resolves the same either way), so this is a record-integrity problem rather than a build problem: the next person reads a config whose two adjacent comments disagree, and a quality document that says a deprecation is fixed when it is not. Would be medium if `baseUrl` were load-bearing for the alias, which it is not on TS 5.x.
findings.summary: baseUrl was not actually dropped; the file now contradicts itself twice
